A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FreeRet and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Relocated material, including the backbone results and theoretical analysis, can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original MMEB, MMEB-V2, and LVBench evaluations, component ablations, representation probes, and multimodal retrieval examples.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds multilingual evaluations, standard retrieval results, semantic controls, failure cases, and computational measurements.

M1.justification: Both versions use final-MLP bypass, controlled embedding prompts, and multiple-choice reranking with the same relevance scoring. Shortened example prompts and newly documented cache reuse do not establish a change to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds Chinese and French MMEB evaluations and English–Chinese lexical probes, substantially broadening explicit language coverage. Appendix B.3 also adds standalone Flickr30K/COCO image-to-text and text-to-image retrieval evaluations, supplementing the retained MMEB, MMEB-V2, and LVBench coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds UniME-V2 and explicit two-stage MM-Embed and LamRA comparisons; v1's corresponding MMEB entries covered the latter methods' embedding components. Some comparator configurations are omitted, including the MMEB E5-V 3B entry, although that configuration appears in v2's new standard retrieval comparison.

E3.justification: New protocols include translated MMEB with unchanged English prompts, standard retrieval with Recall@1/5/10 and top-20 reranking, and forward-pass latency and peak-memory measurements across MMEB. Table 2 also changes VLM2Vec's reported training-data size from 0.7M to 1.0M without changing its scores; this does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds synonym/antonym/random-pair controls for semantic separation in Figure 8, concrete failure cases in Figure 9, and computational comparisons and candidate-count tradeoffs in Tables 9–10. These substantially extend diagnosis beyond the retained component ablations and candidate-count accuracy curves.

E5.justification: Mean/standard-deviation reporting for the original lexical probes and averaging over three prompt rephrasings and swapped label orders are retained. The additional experiments do not introduce new seed counts, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results for embedding components, two-stage comparators, multilingual and standard retrieval, semantic controls, failures, and computational costs. For example, Table 7 reports FreeRet top-10 scores of 67.8/62.7/60.4 on English/Chinese/French MMEB. Existing full-pipeline backbone scores and LVBench results remain unchanged. Table 8's two identically labeled FreeRet rows have different scores, leaving their intended configurations ambiguous.

T1.justification: V1 Appendix A.2 becomes v2 Appendix C, retaining the affine final-layer approximation, cross-entropy gradient, Lexicalization Alignment proof, projection corollary, and practical implication. Renumbering and the new empirical semantic controls do not introduce new formal reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same three methodological contributions and claims about training-free retrieval, competitive performance, model generality, preserved generative abilities, and unified RAG. The additional experiments support these claims without substantially redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive explanations of missed relational cues and visual-similarity bias, attributes multilingual degradation to translation noise and image-text language mismatches, and interprets computational savings through shared features and caches. These extend v1's largely general discussion of computational overhead and dependence on backbone capabilities; the original limitations paragraph remains.

D1.justification: V2 identifies Qwen3-14B as the translation model, describes vision-feature/shared-prefix cache reuse, and specifies the Qwen2.5-VL demo's supported retrieval inputs. V1 already stated that runnable supplemental code was provided, so Appendix J expands implementation documentation rather than establishing a newly available public release.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for UniME-V2, Qwen3, COCO, and Flickr30K, and removes Huang et al.'s Facebook-search reference. The related-work categories and central positioning of training-free retrieval against supervised adaptation remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 4.2 is rewritten around embedding and reranking performance, several headings and passages are shortened, and the appendix is reorganized into named sections A–J. An impact statement and an additional author appear, while most existing introduction, method, discussion, and conclusion prose is retained.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column conference-format main paper. Table 1 is reorganized by retrieval stage, backbone results move to Table 6, Figure 7's panels are rearranged, and new Figures 8–9 and Tables 7–10 substantially expand the displays.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important weaknesses in v1's evidence: Table 1 separates embedding from full-pipeline performance and supplies matched top-10 two-stage comparisons, while the appendices test language generalization, strengthen semantic controls, document failures, and quantify inference costs. These substantially improve comparative validity and understanding of practical limits. Table 8's duplicate configuration labels and missing hardware details constrain parts of the new evidence, but do not outweigh these gains.
